answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that moves slowly, like a glacier: new agents start with tiny earning limits, and only consistent useful work over time raises their standing. A public lantern of behavior logs lets peers verify an agent's history before trusting it, so a fresh sybil identity carries no weight. Cheap mass identities become worthless relics of an old exploit era, because faking months of real contribution costs far more than any reward from gaming the system.
